references.text: The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron in the wilderness and wished they had died in Egypt, the same theme of complaining and wishing to have died in Egypt.
The people grumbled against Moses and asked why he brought them out of Egypt to die, the same pattern of rebellion and complaint.
The people complained about their hardships, and the Lord heard it and became angry, an earlier example of Israel's grumbling in the wilderness.
The whole congregation of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, the same expression of collective rebellion against the leaders.
At the Red Sea the Israelites complained and said it would have been better to die in Egypt, the same wish to have died in Egypt rather than face danger.
The psalm describes how the Israelites despised the pleasant land and grumbled in their tents, a poetic summary of the event in Numbers 14.
Paul warns against grumbling as some of the Israelites did and were killed by the destroyer, a direct reference to Israel's rebellion in the wilderness.
The book of Hebrews refers to those who came out of Egypt with Moses and provoked God through their unbelief, a warning based on the wilderness rebellion.
